what_its_for: Nilotinib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of blood cancer called chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). It works by blocking a protein that tells cancer cells to grow, which helps slow or stop the cancer from spreading.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT open, crush, or chew the capsules. Take this medicine on an empty stomach — do not eat anything for at least 2 hours before your dose and at least 1 hour after your dose. This is very important because food can cause too much of the medicine to enter your body, which can be dangerous.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition. The typical adult dose is 300 mg to 400 mg taken twice daily, about 12 hours apart. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose or stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regularly scheduled time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time or take an extra dose to make up for the one you missed. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store nilotinib at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Store in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medicines down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your body and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid eating for 2 hours before and 1 hour after each dose. Tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because many drugs can interact with nilotinib — especially antacids, heart medicines, and certain antibiotics or antifungals. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as your skin may be more sensitive. Do not drive or use heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or faint.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain, shortness of breath, or a fast or irregular heartbeat; sudden numbness, weakness, or severe headache (signs of stroke); severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual bleeding or bruising; fever, chills, or signs of infection; fainting or dizziness; swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles; or any rash or skin reaction. These could be signs of serious side effects that need immediate attention.
when_it_works: Nilotinib starts working right away in your body, but you may not feel different immediately. Most people begin to see improvements in their blood test results within a few weeks to months. It may take several months to see the full benefit of the medicine. It is very important to keep taking it every day, even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use nilotinib if you are pregnant, as it can harm your unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 14 days after your last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Children: Nilotinib may be used in children aged 1 year and older for certain types of CML; your child's doctor will determine the right dose. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects and should be monitored closely. Liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
